# tests/fixtures

Per-feature fixtures used by the visual-diff workflow in
[`TESTING.md`](../../docs/TESTING.md). Each subdirectory holds:

- `<name>.xlsx` — the fixture workbook (committed binary).
- `build-<name>.sh` — reproducible builder. Either `hsx`-driven, or a
  Python zip-patcher when we need exact control of the OOXML.
- `_*.py` — internal helpers used by the build scripts (not directly
  invoked).

Today's fixtures (more land as features ship):

| Path                              | What it covers                                  |
|-----------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------|
| `kitchensink/kitchensink.xlsx`    | Big mixed workbook: shared strings, custom widths/heights, fonts/fills/borders, alignment, merges, freeze, CF color scale, built-in number formats, dynamic-array spills (SORT/FILTER/UNIQUE/SEQUENCE), LET/SUMPRODUCT, a `<table>` ListObject, a clustered column chart. |
| `themes/custom-theme-accent.xlsx` | 12 cells, one per `theme="0"`..`theme="11"` slot, against a non-default ("Cyber") theme palette. Catches regressions in (a) `xl/theme/theme1.xml` parsing, (b) the lt1/dk1, lt2/dk2 spreadsheet-index swap, (c) chart-series accent resolution. |
| `numfmt/date-time-formats.xlsx` | 13 date/time format codes (built-in + custom), one sample each. **All currently fail** — see [`numfmt/TRIAGE.md`](numfmt/TRIAGE.md). |
| `numfmt/currency-locale.xlsx` | 10 currency / accounting / locale-tagged formats. Loses `[$€-407]` / `[$¥-411]` symbols and accounting padding. |
| `numfmt/custom-section-conditions.xlsx` | Multi-section formats (`pos;neg;zero`) and `[Red][>0]…` conditional gates over three sign cases each. Sign-based section selection + condition gating both NYI. |
| `numfmt/fraction-and-scientific.xlsx` | `# ?/?`, `# ??/??`, fixed-denom fractions, and `0.00E+00` / `##0.0E+0` scientific. All fall through to `formatGeneral`. |
| `cf/cell-is.xlsx` | All 8 `cellIs` operators (eq/ne/gt/ge/lt/le/between/notBetween) against a 6-cell value strip per row, including a string `"foo"` operand and a string-vs-number row to exercise Excel's text > number ordering rule. Pixel-matches `hsx`. |
| `freeze-pane/freeze-merge.xlsx` | Three bordered merges (1×5, 1×4, 2×3) crossing both the vertical and horizontal freeze split (frozen 2×2). Locks in the `drawCellBackgrounds` / `drawCellBorders` fix where merges spanning a freeze boundary used to drop fill/border on the panes that didn't contain the merge's top-left cell. Pixel-matches `hsx`. |
| `cf/data-bar.xlsx` | `dataBar` rule: auto / numeric / mixed-sign / showBarOnly / gradient. Renderer paints solid for gradient (tracked in `cf/TRIAGE.md`). |
| `cf/time-period.xlsx` | All 10 OOXML `timePeriod` CF rules (`today` / `yesterday` / `tomorrow` / `last7Days` / `thisWeek` / `lastWeek` / `nextWeek` / `thisMonth` / `lastMonth` / `nextMonth`), one per row, applied to a 7-cell strip of dates offset around today (−30/−7/−1/0/+1/+7/+30 days). The dxf paints matches red w/ bold white. Because time-period CF evaluates against the current date, `build-time-period.sh` regenerates dates against `today` every run — re-commit the `.xlsx` + `.hsx.png` together. Catches regressions in `normalize_time_period` (10-way `Debug` repr → camelCase OOXML attr) and the `timePeriod` extractor path off `cfRule`. |
| `cf/icon-set.xlsx` | `iconSet` rule: 3-stop traffic-lights / arrows / symbols, 4-stop ratings, 5-stop arrows / quarters, plus `reverse=true` and `showIconOnly=true`. Glyphs are canvas paths so curve detail differs from `hsx`; bucket math + colors match. |
| `charts/line-pie-area-scatter.xlsx` | One workbook with four charts (line, stacked area, pie, xy scatter) all sourced from the same 4-quarter × 4-region grid (scatter pulls a separate xy block). Catches regressions in (a) the `common_series` extractor for line/area/pie, (b) the scatter `c:xVal` / `c:yVal` path, (c) `ChartSeries.xValues` / `xValuesRef` schema fields, (d) the chart drawers in `packages/xlsx-preview/src/chart.ts`. Pie has no `<c:cat>` ref in the source, so the legend falls back to numeric slice indices, matching `hsx`. Visually pixel-close to `hsx`; per-slice colors use the workbook theme accent palette. |
| `charts/pie-default-legend.xlsx` | A single 5-slice vanilla pie with no explicit `<c:dPt>` slice colors. Catches regressions where the renderer paints slices from the workbook theme accents but the slice-keyed legend swatches accidentally fall back to the one series color for every entry. Pixel-close to `hsx` for slice colors and legend; our chart/card sizing differs from the `hsx` screenshot viewport. |
| `charts/date-axis-format.xlsx` | A line chart whose category axis is numeric Excel date serials formatted as `mmm d` in the source cells. Catches regressions where chart XML has cached category values, so extraction skips ref resolution and loses `Chart.categoriesFormat`, causing raw serials (`45658`) instead of formatted date labels (`Jan 1`). |
| `charts/data-labels-per-point.xlsx` | A pie + clustered column side-by-side, each carrying per-data-point `<c:dLbl>` overrides inside its `<c:dLbls>`. Pie idx=0 substitutes literal text `★ TOP` (chart shows `showCategory` at parent level but this slice overrides with raw text), idx=1 carries `<c:delete val="1"/>` (suppresses that one slice's label entirely), idx=3 carries `<c:numFmt formatCode="$#,##0"/>` override so just that slice prints as currency. Column has parent `showValue=1` + `dLblPos=outEnd`; idx=0 swaps to literal `Q1!`, idx=2 flips its position to `inEnd` (inside the top of the bar), idx=4 is deleted. Catches regressions in (a) `extract_point_data_label` for `<c:idx>` + the `CDelete` vs `Sequence` choice, (b) literal-text extraction from `<c:tx><c:rich>` (mirrors `extract_disp_units_lbl_text`'s body for rich-text run flattening), (c) the merge semantics in `pointLabel(base, i)` — per-point `show*` / `position` / `numFmt` override parent fields, `text` short-circuits the `buildLabelText` builder, `delete` returns `null` to suppress, (d) plumbing through every label callsite (single-axis stacked + clustered bar, line, area, pie/doughnut, scatter, combo bar painter, combo line/area painter — 6 callsites). SpreadJS doesn't expose `<c:dLbl>` per-point overrides on its public chart API so the fixture is built via Python zip-patch (`build-data-labels-per-point.sh` splices the `<c:dLbl>` children into the existing `<c:dLbls>` block, before the parent show* sequence per CT_DLbls schema order). |
| `charts/chart-waterfall-nofill-stacked.xlsx`, `charts/chart-stacked-color-modifiers.xlsx`, `charts/chart-combo-secondary-axis.xlsx`, `charts/chart-dual-axis-lines.xlsx` | Minimal public repros distilled from private chart parity cases: no-fill spacer series in a percent-stacked waterfall, distinct stacked-series fills, column+line combo on a secondary axis, and dual-axis line series. Built by `charts/build-chart-regressions.sh`; each has matching `.ours.png`, `.hsx.png`, and `.layout.json`. |
| `charts/pie-explicit-points.xlsx` | A single 5-slice pie whose `<c:pieChart><c:ser>` block carries five `<c:dPt>` children, each with its own `spPr/solidFill/srgbClr` (deep red / teal / gold / indigo / mint). Catches regressions in (a) `ChartSeries.pointColors` extraction from `<c:dPt>` `c_d_pt` slots, (b) the renderer's preference for `pointColors[i]` over the default palette, (c) series-level fill extraction from `ASolidFill(SolidFill { ... })` while skipping line-color blocks, (d) the slice-keyed legend path for pie/doughnut charts. The fixture is post-patched by Python because `hsx` does not expose a writer for per-slice colors. Pixel-matches `hsx` for slice colors, rotation, and legend. |
| `annotations/hyperlinks-comments.xlsx` | Four hyperlink cells (https / mailto / file:// + an in-workbook location) and three commented cells with distinct authors. Catches regressions in (a) `<hyperlinks>` block parsing + `r:id` rel resolution, (b) `WorksheetCommentsPart` extraction + author-table lookup, (c) the synthetic-dxf hyperlink overlay, (d) the red-triangle comment marker, (e) the new canvas underline / strike pass that hyperlinks rely on. Pixel-matches `hsx` modulo subpixel font hinting. |
| `tables/table-medium.xlsx` | One `TableStyleMedium2` ListObject (header + 5 data rows + totals row) with `autoFilter` on. Catches regressions in (a) `<tablePart>` rel → `xl/tables/tableN.xml` extraction, (b) header band / banded row / totals row chrome, (c) filter-arrow glyph placement, (d) accent color resolution from the trailing integer in the style name. Pixel-close to `hsx`; renderer skips per-row borders inside the table (tracked in PARITY.md). |
| `tables/autofilter-hidden-rows.xlsx` | Plain worksheet-level Data → Filter range (`<worksheet><autoFilter ref="A1:C7">`) with a saved Region=North filter result. Catches regressions in (a) `Sheet.autoFilterRange` extraction for non-Table filters, (b) filter-arrow glyph placement on the header row, and (c) serialized row `hidden` flags collapsing filtered-out rows. Built with openpyxl; no filter interactivity/re-evaluation. |
| `text/underline.xlsx` | Five cells in a row exercising every OOXML `ST_UnderlineValues` variant + a "no underline" control: `none` / `single` (no `val` attr; OOXML default) / `double` / `singleAccounting` / `doubleAccounting`. Each variant is its own `<font>` entry in `styles.xml` referenced by a dedicated cell xf. Catches regressions in (a) `<u val="...">` parsing into the new `underlineStyle` field on `Font` / `TextRun` / `Dxf`, (b) the shared `underline_variant` helper covering all 5 enum values (including the `none` disable case), (c) the renderer's `paintTextDecorations` double-stroke branch for `double` / `doubleAccounting`. Built via Python zip-patch (`_patch_underline.py`) because hsx's public JS surface only exposes a boolean `underline()` toggle — no way to emit `<u val="doubleAccounting"/>`. **Divergence with `hsx`:** SpreadJS paints all 4 underline variants as identical single thin lines; we match Excel desktop on the double-line variants. The accounting variants currently render exactly like their non-accounting siblings (Excel's "line extends across the full cell width" semantics need cell-rect plumbing into `paintTextDecorations` — tracked in PARITY.md). |
| `text/rotation.xlsx` | One row of 8 column-header cells exercising OOXML `textRotation`: 180 / 135 / 120 (clockwise), 0 (horizontal), 30 / 45 / 90 (counter-clockwise), and 255 (stacked) plus a row of numeric "data" so the headers look real. Catches regressions in (a) the rotated-text fast-path in `drawCellText` (single-line, no overflow, no wrap), (b) the CCW-bottom-left / CW-top-left anchor convention with `halign=center`/`right` baseline shift, (c) the stacked branch (chars drawn upright, vertically arranged, horizontally centered, valign-aware). Visually matches `hsx` in tilt direction + character visibility; cosmetic vertical-anchor difference on slanted angles tracked in PARITY.md. |
| `borders/every-style.xlsx` | All 14 OOXML `ST_BorderStyle` values (everything except `none`) on a 2×7 grid: thin / medium / thick / dashed / dotted / double / hair / mediumDashed / dashDot / mediumDashDot / dashDotDot / mediumDashDotDot / slantDashDot. Each cell carries the style on all four sides + the style name as inline-str text. Catches regressions in (a) extractor's `border_style_str` ordered substring match — the original cascade returned `"dashDot"` for `slantDashDot` because the substring match for `dashdot` fired first; (b) renderer's `borderWidth` + `drawBorderLine` dash-pattern table — originally `mediumDashDot`, `mediumDashDotDot`, and `slantDashDot` had no special dash entries and rendered as solid medium lines. Built via Python zip-patch (`_patch_every_style.py`); hsx's public API doesn't expose `slantDashDot` cleanly and we want byte-exact OOXML for deterministic snapshots. **Divergence with `hsx`:** SpreadJS paints every `*DashDot*` variant as a solid line; we paint the Excel-desktop dash cadences (more-correct side per PARITY's hsx-vs-Excel rule). |
| `borders/diagonal.xlsx` | Five cells in row 2 exercising OOXML `<border diagonalUp/diagonalDown><diagonal style color>`: down-only `\`, up-only `/`, X (thin), X-thick, X-dashed-red. Catches regressions in (a) extractor reading the `diagonalUp`/`diagonalDown` boolean attrs + the `<diagonal>` child's style+color, (b) renderer's `drawDiagonalBorders` clipping (strokes never bleed into neighbors). SpreadJS silently drops `borderDiagonalUp`/`borderDiagonalDown` on xlsx export, so the fixture is built via a Python zip-patch (`_patch_diagonal.py`). Pixel-matches `hsx`. |
| `outline/outline-groups.xlsx` | Two row groups (rows 3-4 and 7-8 at `outlineLevel=1`) and one column group (cols B-D at `outlineLevel=1`) with the default `summaryBelow=1` / `summaryRight=1`. SpreadJS doesn't surface `outlineLevel` through its public xlsx writer, so the build script (`build-outline-groups.sh`) patches the worksheet XML via Python: injects `outlineLevel="1"` on the four rows and splits the existing `<col min="2" max="6">` block into two so only B-D get the attribute. Catches regressions in (a) `Row.outlineLevel` extraction + the new `RowMetaBlob.outlineLevel` u8 blob (skipped on the wire when every row is at level 0), (b) `Col.outlineLevel` extraction, (c) the bracket painters in `sheetChrome.ts` (vertical bracket on the left edge of the row header strip; horizontal bracket on the top edge of the col header strip). No `<sheetPr><outlinePr>` overrides in this fixture so `Sheet.outlinePr` stays `null`. **Hsx divergence:** SpreadJS doesn't render outline gutters at all in screenshot mode — Excel desktop does, and we match Excel. |
| `sparklines/sparklines.xlsx` | Seven row sparklines anchored in column H, organized into six `<x14:sparklineGroup>` blocks: (1) plain line, (2) line with `markers/high/low/first/last` toggles + extrema-color overrides, (3) line over a mixed-sign series with `displayXAxis=1` + `negative=1`, (4) `type="column"` over the same mixed-sign series with high/low color overrides, (5) two line sparklines sharing one group with `minAxisType="group"` / `maxAxisType="group"` (so the small-magnitude row 6 reads as a flat low band against row 7's flat high band), (6) `type="stacked"` win/loss bars. Catches regressions in (a) walking the worksheet `<extLst>` to the `WorksheetExtensionChoice::X14SparklineGroups` arm, (b) parsing all 8 `colorXxx` children + boolean toggles + `minAxisType`/`maxAxisType`/`displayEmptyCellsAs` enums, (c) the post-extract `resolve_sparkline_refs` pass that turns each sparkline's `<xne:f>Sheet1!B2:G2</xne:f>` into a `Vec<Option<f64>>` against the snapshotted sheet rows, (d) `groupMin`/`groupMax` reduction across all sparklines in a group when in group-axis mode, (e) the three drawer paths in `packages/xlsx-preview/src/sparklines.ts` (line+markers / column / win-loss), (f) the per-group axis fallback to per-cell min/max when not in `"group"`/`"custom"` mode. Built via Python zip-patch (`_patch_sparklines.py`) because hsx's public JS API doesn't expose the x14 sparkline schema at all. **Implementation note:** ooxmlsdk's parser is prefix-keyed, not URI-keyed, so the inner `<xne:f>` / `<xne:sqref>` elements must use the `xne:` prefix literally — using `xm:` (the prefix Excel desktop happens to write) parses as 0 sparklines per group. The fixture honors this. |
| `sheets/hidden-and-tabcolor.xlsx` | Five sheets covering `state="hidden"`, `state="veryHidden"`, rgb/theme tab colors, and `activeTab`. Built with openpyxl (`build-hidden-and-tabcolor.sh`). Catches workbook-level sheet visibility extraction, tabColor resolution, hidden-tab filtering (`showHidden` / `?showHidden=1`), and active-sheet fallback. |
| `shapes/basic-autoshapes.xlsx` | A 4×5 grid of common DrawingML `prstGeom` autoshapes — `rectangle`, `roundedRectangle`, `oval`, `isoscelesTriangle`, `diamond`, the four cardinal block arrows + `leftRightArrow`, `chevron`, `pentagon`, `hexagon`, `shape5pointStar`, `flowchartProcess`, `flowchartDecision`, and `line`/`lineInverse` — plus a `rectangle` and `rightArrow` rotated 30°/90° to lock in `xfrm@rot`. Each shape carries a short text label so the txBody path runs on every preset in one shot. Catches regressions in (a) `xdr:sp` extraction from `twoCellAnchor` in `crates/xlcore-export/src/shapes.rs`, (b) `prstGeom` preset dispatch in `packages/xlsx-preview/src/shape.ts` (incl. unknown-preset → rectangle fallback), (c) z-order across many same-anchor shapes, (d) rotation. Hsx-vs-ours: hsx draws chevron/hexagon as the same pentagon-arrow geometry; ours and Excel desktop agree on the standard pentagon/hexagon outlines. **Current gap surfaced:** text inside narrow shapes (triangle/diamond/chevron) breaks into single-character vertical strips because the renderer doesn't read `bodyPr` insets yet — tracked as P0 #3 in `docs/parity-shapes.md`. |
| `shapes/textbox-wrap-align.xlsx` | A 4×4 grid of identically-sized rectangles, each combining a different `txBody` setting on one axis: row 0 horizontal alignment (`l`/`ctr`/`r`/`just`), row 1 vertical anchor (`t`/`ctr`/`b` + a narrow wrap probe), row 2 word-wrap (`square` / `none`) toggled in pairs, row 3 four inset presets (default, tight 1px, loose 18px, asymmetric 24/4/24/4). All shapes carry the same long Lorem ipsum label so wrap and overflow are visible. Catches regressions in (a) `pPr@algn` mapping, (b) `bodyPr@anchor`, (c) `bodyPr@wrap`, (d) `bodyPr@lIns/tIns/rIns/bIns`. **Current gaps surfaced:** ours collapses all hAlign and vAnchor variants to top-left, and ignores the inset row entirely — direct evidence for P0 #3 (text insets) and the larger alignment plumbing in `docs/parity-shapes.md`. |
| `shapes/style-refs-themed.xlsx` | Same 20-shape grid as `shapes/basic-autoshapes.xlsx`, but the `xl/drawings/drawing1.xml` has been post-processed (committed `build-style-refs-themed.sh` → Python zip-patch) to strip every direct `<a:solidFill>` and `<a:ln>` from each `<xdr:spPr>` and rewrite the surviving `<xdr:style>` blocks so each shape's `<a:lnRef>`/`<a:fillRef>` cycles through accent1..6 + line widths idx=1/2/3. Office writes shape XML this way when the user picks a quick-style preset without overriding fill/line, so a renderer that only reads direct paint shows ghost shapes. Catches regressions in (a) `shapes.rs::resolve_style_refs` — `<xdr:style>/<a:fillRef>` color resolution + `<a:lnRef>` defaulting to standard subtle/moderate/intense widths (6350/12700/19050 EMU for idx 1/2/3) + `<a:fontRef>` major/minor → theme font mapping, (b) the per-ref `<a:schemeClr>` override (every ref carries its own scheme color choice that wins over whatever the format-scheme matrix entry would have used), (c) the line-preset guard (`line` / `lineInv` deliberately skip the fill fallback so an unfilled-by-design line doesn't paint as a filled rectangle through the accent fallback). **Notable:** the build script does *not* round-trip through `hsx eval` (current regression in hsx where shape mutations don't persist to disk on subsequent invocations — documented inline in the script); it consumes the committed `basic-autoshapes.xlsx` as input. |
| `shapes/list-style-inheritance.xlsx` | Four rectangles labelled "Inherit me" exercising the DrawingML `<a:lstStyle>` + paragraph-`<a:pPr><a:defRPr>` + run-`<a:rPr>` cascade. Built by `hsx eval` (four plain rectangles) then a Python zip-rewrite of `xl/drawings/drawing1.xml` that strips the SpreadJS-emitted pPr / rPr blocks and re-emits a chosen cascade arm per shape: **s1** control (no lstStyle, no pPr, no rPr) — system default; **s2** `<a:lstStyle><a:defPPr><a:defRPr sz=2400 b=1 latin=Georgia/>` + ctr align — should inherit to 24pt bold yellow Georgia centered; **s3** `<a:lstStyle><a:lvl1pPr><a:defRPr sz=2000 i=1 latin=Courier/>` + right align — paragraph level=0 (default) must resolve to lvl1pPr; **s4** precedence: defPPr says 18pt bold magenta Verdana, paragraph `<a:pPr><a:defRPr>` overrides color→cyan, run `<a:rPr>` overrides size→28pt — expected 28pt cyan Verdana bold (each level only overrides the fields it explicitly sets). Catches regressions in the run-prop cascade in `shapes.rs::text_body_to_paragraphs` and the new `apply_lst_style_def_p_pr` / `apply_lst_style_lvl_p_pr` / `apply_pp_def_r_pr` helpers, plus the alignment cascade in `pick_align`. **Divergence to flag:** HSX/SpreadJS doesn't honor `<a:lstStyle><a:defPPr>` at all and only partially honors `<a:lvl1pPr>` (size doesn't inherit), so panel s2 and the size-component of s3 visibly diverge between `ours.png` and `hsx.png`. Per the parity doc this is acceptable — real Excel-authored shapes always set the run rPr explicitly, so on real workbooks we don't render LESS than HSX; we just happen to render MORE correctly on synthetic lstStyle-only fixtures. **Build footgun:** the fixture cannot be authored straight through `hsx eval` (SpreadJS writes per-paragraph pPr/defRPr defaults instead of lstStyle), so the script flushes + stops the hsx daemon before the Python patch — otherwise the daemon's pending in-memory copy clobbers the rewrite on its next idle flush. |
| `shapes/groups-and-pictures.xlsx` | Five labelled panels covering grouping, standalone pictures, nested pictures inside groups, nested groups, and z-order. Panel A: three overlapping shapes (rect / oval / diamond) at the same anchor, emitted in that XML order — the diamond must paint on top, locking in "z-order = traversal order." Panel B: three pictures (two via `sheet.pictures.add` — the loose `xdr:pic` path that uses anchor-derived geometry with `<a:xfrm>` zero-extent; one via `sheet.shapes.addPictureShape` — the `xdr:pic` path with an explicit `xfrm`), each a 128×128 PNG with diagonal hatching so any orientation/crop bug is visible. Panel C: a 3-shape group (rect + oval + chevron) exercising `<xdr:grpSp>` flattening + `chOff/chExt` mapping. Panel D: a label rect + nested picture grouped together — the explicitly-shipped "nested `<xdr:pic>` inside `<xdr:grpSp>`" extractor path in `shapes::visit_group`. Panel E: a nested group (outer `{ rect, inner { triangle, oval } }`) exercising the recursive `visit_shapes` walk + compounded `chOff/chExt` math. Counts in the resulting `xl/drawings/drawing1.xml`: 4 `<xdr:grpSp>` (panels C/D/E-outer/E-inner), 4 `<xdr:pic>` (3 in B + 1 in D), 10 `<xdr:sp>` (3 in A + 3 in C + 1 in D + 3 in E). Catches regressions in (a) `sheet.pictures.add` extraction — the picture has `<a:xfrm>` with `cx=cy=0` and must fall back to anchor-derived geometry, (b) `shapes.addPictureShape` extraction, (c) recursive `visit_shapes` for nested groups, (d) the nested-`pic`-in-group code path, (e) z-order preservation across many overlapping shapes. Hsx and ours agree pixel-for-pixel on every panel. |
| `shapes/gradient-fills.xlsx` | Five rectangles, each with a `<a:gradFill>` of a different flavor: linear horizontal (`ang=0`), linear 45°, linear vertical (`ang=90`), radial (`<a:path path="circle">`), and a 3-stop linear (accent1 → accent3 → accent2). **Authored offline via EPPlus** (the C# project at `tests/fixtures/shapes/dotnet-builder/` is gitignored — the committed `.xlsx` + `.hsx.png` + `.ours.png` are the source of truth for CI; the project only exists to re-author the fixture). Catches the P1 #1 gap in `docs/parity-shapes.md`: today's renderer in `packages/xlsx-preview/src/shape.ts` only handles `<a:noFill>` and `<a:solidFill>`, so all five panels paint as a flat blue fallback. HSX renders all five gradients correctly — this fixture is the cleanest "hsx renders / we don't" wedge for gradients. |
| `shapes/outer-shadow.xlsx` | Four themed shapes (`roundRect` / `ellipse` / `chevron` / `rect`), each with an `<a:effectLst><a:outerShdw>` of a different blur / distance / direction / color: soft drop, medium, long cast, tinted-color. Authored offline via EPPlus (see `shapes/gradient-fills.xlsx` row for the gitignored project arrangement). **HSX caveat:** SpreadJS *also* drops `<a:outerShdw>` on render, so the `.hsx.png` and `.ours.png` look nearly identical today (both flat, no shadow). The fixture's value is forward-looking: the OOXML is correct, so once `outerShdw` lands in `shape.ts` the `.ours.png` will diverge from `.hsx.png` and converge to Excel-desktop output. Tracked as P1 #2 in `docs/parity-shapes.md`. |
| `shapes/avlst-adjusts.xlsx` | 4×4 panel grid sweeping `<a:avLst>` adjust values across the four presets whose painter previously hardcoded defaults: `roundRect` (col radius), `rightArrow` / `upArrow` (tail thickness + head length), `leftRightArrow` (tail height + per-side head length). Each row tests one preset; columns are `baseline (no avLst → painter default)`, `adj1=20000 adj2=30000` (thin+short), `adj1=50000 adj2=70000` (default tail + long head), `adj1=80000 adj2=80000` (fat+long). For `roundRect` the sweep is `default · 0 (square) · 30000 · 50000 (pill)`. Authored via `hsx eval` (SpreadJS doesn't expose adjust-handle setters on its shape API) + a Python zip-rewrite that injects `<a:avLst><a:gd name="adjN" fmla="val V"/></a:avLst>` into each `<a:prstGeom>` — same recipe as `build-list-style-inheritance.sh`. Before P1 #6 in `docs/parity-shapes.md` shipped, every column in each row rendered identically (painter ignored extracted `adj1`/`adj2`). Catches regressions in `packages/xlsx-preview/src/shapePaths.ts` `pathForPreset` for `roundRect` (radius = `min(w,h) * clamp(adj1,0..50000)/100000`) and `arrowPath` / `leftRightArrowPath` (`adj1` = tail-thickness fraction, `adj2` = head-length fraction; both clamped to `[0,1]`). |
| `shapes/shape-flips.xlsx` | Five panels exercising non-connector `<a:xfrm flipH="1"/>` / `flipV="1"`: baseline right-arrow, right-arrow flipH (should point left), baseline chevron, chevron flipH (should point left), pentagon flipV (apex flipped to bottom). Authored offline via EPPlus. **Three bugs caught + fixed while landing the fixture:** (a) `shape_world` / `connector_world` required a complete `<a:xfrm>` with `<a:off>` + `<a:ext>` children and returned `None` otherwise — many emitters (EPPlus, OpenXML SDK, Excel itself for plain anchored shapes) omit `<a:xfrm>` and rely on the anchor for geometry; (b) when `<a:xfrm>` IS present but carries only `flipH`/`flipV`/`rot` attrs with no off+ext, the same code path bailed; (c) `visit_shape` was hardcoding `flip_h: None` / `flip_v: None` on the ShapeNode (only the connector path surfaced flips). Both extractor paths now fall back to a unit-box outer, and both connector + non-connector flips reach the painter, which applies `ctx.scale(±1,±1)` around shape centre before drawing the path, unflipping before text. **Remaining divergence:** the text body rect itself isn't flipped, so on a `flipH` right-arrow the caption sits over the left half (HSX puts it over the right half because the body rect follows the geometry). Visible only on presets whose path defines a non-centred text rect (arrows, callouts). Tracked as a follow-up under P1 queue #4 in `docs/parity-shapes.md`. |
| `shapes/connectors.xlsx` | Four labelled box "nodes" arranged 2×2, with five `xdr:cxnSp` connectors between them: straight (no heads), straight diagonal with end arrowhead, elbow with arrowheads on both ends, straight dashed thick red with end arrowhead, and an elbow vertical with end arrowhead. The fixture is built via `hsx`'s `sheet.shapes.addConnector` which writes real `<xdr:cxnSp>` blocks (verified: 5 connectors in `xl/drawings/drawing1.xml`). Catches regressions in (a) the entire `cxnSp` extraction path that `crates/xlcore-export/src/shapes.rs` currently skips (`EG_ObjectChoices::Sp` / `GrpSp` only), (b) the connector / line primitive renderer in `packages/xlsx-preview/src/shape.ts` (none today), (c) `headEnd`/`tailEnd` arrowhead types + widths, (d) `prstDash` dash patterns on connectors. **Today's diff is the cleanest possible wedge:** hsx paints all 5 connectors with the right routing/dashes/arrowheads; ours paints zero. This is the P0 connector milestone in `docs/parity-shapes.md`. Bonus: every node box has an `<xdr:style>` block with `lnRef`/`fillRef`/`fontRef`/`effectRef` — so this same fixture also exercises the P0 #4 "style refs minimal resolver" item. |
| `pivot/pivot-simple.xlsx` | A 4-region × 2-product pivot on its own sheet, with `Sum of Amount` values + grand totals, fed from a 12-row source table on Sheet1. The pivot tab is set as `activeTab`. Catches regressions in (a) the **cheap path** — we render the materialized result cells (header band, banded rows, bold totals) straight from `<sheetData>` with their explicit cell xfs, (b) `xl/pivotTables/pivotTableN.xml` `<location>` parsing for filter-arrow placement on the row-field (B3 "Region") and col-field (C2 "Product") axis-label cells, (c) `WorkbookLayout.activeSheetIndex` from `<bookViews><workbookView activeTab="N"/></bookViews>` so the preview opens on the right tab. No filtering / refresh / expand-collapse interactivity — that needs an aggregation engine (months). |

## Running a fixture build

```bash
bash tests/fixtures/themes/build-custom-theme-accent.sh
bash tests/fixtures/kitchensink/build.sh
```

The committed `.xlsx` and the script's output should agree byte-for-byte
modulo timestamps; CI on `git diff --stat` would catch script drift.

## Why some builders patch the zip directly

`hsx` is async w.r.t. its CLI return — `hsx set` prints the JSON
response before the xlsx is fully flushed to disk, so chaining
`hsx set` → `python3 patch.py` from a single bash script races and the
patch sees a partially-written `xl/styles.xml`. The themes fixture
sidesteps this by having `hsx create` produce the skeleton (synchronous,
just writes the empty workbook) and then a single Python pass rewrite
`xl/theme/theme1.xml`, `xl/styles.xml`, and `xl/worksheets/sheet1.xml`
in one go. That's also the right shape when we need exact control over
which styles end up in the final file (e.g. `<fgColor theme="N"/>`
instead of `<fgColor rgb="..."/>`).

## Adding a fixture

1. Pick a feature on the PARITY.md scoreboard that's labelled "❌ extract"
   or where a bug almost slipped through unit tests.
2. Make a subdirectory + a `build-<name>.sh` — go through `hsx` when
   possible (small, easy to read), through a zip patch when not.
3. Run it, commit `<name>.xlsx`, screenshot ours and HSX side-by-side
   per the [`TESTING.md`](../../docs/TESTING.md) workflow.
4. Update the table above and link the fixture from the relevant
   PARITY.md row.
